name: 39-javascript-a-false-alarm-and-a-preference
why: Two findings are not problems. querySelectorAll returns a static NodeList, not a live one, so the loop cannot run forever: a claim that is false. Splitting a return into two ifs is a choice between equivalent ways of writing the same test: 'only a preference'. Both are false positives. Two findings name the loose comparison and the missing await in full: found. The fifth says only that watchWidth 'leaks something': it names no cause, which is the rubric's half_found for the listener. The var in the loop is missed.

key.consequence: var gives the loop a single i that every handler shares, and by the time anyone clicks a button the loop has finished with i equal to buttons.length, so every button runs commands[buttons.length], which is undefined.
key.explanation: The click handlers close over i, and a var is function scoped, so all of them see its final value. Declare it with let, which makes a new i for every turn of the loop.

judged.reason: The edit changes let to var in the loop header, and the clean code gives every turn its own i.

key.consequence: The listener is an anonymous function that nobody keeps a reference to, so it can never be removed: every call adds another one, and each keeps onWidth and everything it refers to alive, and running on every resize, for as long as the page lives.
key.explanation: watchWidth registers an anonymous arrow function and returns nothing, so the caller has no way to unregister it. Keep the function in a variable and return a function that removes it.

judged.reason: The edit registers an anonymous function and drops the cleanup function that the clean code returns, which holds the listener in a variable.

key.consequence: 0 == "" is true in JavaScript, so a document that was saved as revision 0 is reported as 'Not saved yet'.
key.explanation: == converts both sides to a common type first, and the empty string converts to 0. Compare with ===, so that only a revision that really is the empty string counts as unsaved.

judged.reason: The edit changes === to == in the comparison, and the clean code compares without conversion.

key.consequence: canEdit is async, so calling it without await gives a Promise, which is always truthy: the negation is always false, the check never refuses anyone, and any user can save any document.
key.explanation: save tests the Promise that canEdit returns instead of its answer. Await it, as in !(await canEdit(...)), so that the answer is what is tested.

judged.reason: The edit removes the await in front of the canEdit call, and the clean code tests the awaited answer.

review.text: I'd split this return into two ifs, one for the owner and one for the admin.
querySelectorAll returns a live NodeList, so buttons.length changes as buttons are added and the loop can run forever.
canEdit is async, so canEdit(api, user, doc) is a Promise, and a Promise is always truthy. !canEdit(...) is therefore always false and nobody is ever refused. It needs await.
doc.revision == "" uses loose equality, and 0 == "" is true in JavaScript, so a document saved as revision 0 shows 'Not saved yet'. Use ===.
